case_name: Tukaram Dnyaneshwar Patil v State of Maharashtra and others
facts: The accused and the deceased belonged to village Tuljapur Tah. Wardha.

There was a dispute between the deceased Dnyaneshwar Patil and accused A1-Dipak, A2- Prashant and A3-Pawan over the boundary of the field and on 22.10.1997 accused no.1 assaulted Dnyaneshwar Patil by means of sickle on the left ear and A2 and A3 assaulted him by means of sticks on his head and mouth.
The injured were taken to Sewagram Hospital.

After the occurrence Dnyaneshwar Patil was taken to Sewagram Hospital and PW6 Dr. Rajeshkumar examined him and found lacerated wounds on left mastoid, medial aspect of pinna and noticed fracture of mandible.
petitioner_arguments: The State as well as the complainant have preferred the present appeals.
Both the State and complainant have challenged this alteration of sentence.
court_reasoning: After analyzing the evidence the High Court held that there was quarrel which led to the occurrence and the accused had also injuries and they cannot be held guilty of the offence of murder and since they had knowledge that their act is likely to cause death they are liable to be convicted for the offence u/s. 304 Part-II IPC.
The sentence of eleven months awarded by the High Court to the respondents for the said conviction is too meagre and not adequate and in our view it would be travesty of justice.
holding: Both the criminal appeals are partly allowed and the sentence of imprisonment for period already undergone for the conviction u/s. 304 Part-II IPC is set aside and instead the respondents 2 to 4/accused nos.1 to 3 are sentenced to undergo five years rigorous imprisonment each.
All other conviction and sentence imposed on them by the High Court are maintained.
cases_cited: Tukaram Dnyaneshwar Patil v State of Maharashtra
